ambiguity_log.where: section 11.2 step 2, an inclusion path that does not fit
ambiguity_log.reading: a proof whose path is too short or too long for its tree_size and leaf_index (RFC 9162 section 2.1.3.2 ends with sn != 0) gives no candidate root and so does not authenticate the target; it is not read as ReceiptMalformed, which P2 reserves for unreadable proofs and leaf_index >= tree_size
a leaf is checked when its COSE_Sign1 array is readable, tagged or untagged ("detection needs the COSE_Sign1 array to be readable"); an unreadable leaf makes no domain claim

ambiguity_log.where: section 9.1 P4, two Invalid codes at once
ambiguity_log.reading: a duplicate index and an index beyond n in the same request: DuplicateIndex is reported first, as the phase table lists it first; the text orders phases, not codes inside one

each of the four LogIdentityV0 components is compared by a more specific code (TsIssuerMismatch at P7, the key fingerprint at P0, the VDS at P0 and P3, LeafSpecDigestMismatch at P7), and the physical request has no expected_log_identity_digest; so this reading never emits LogIdentityInconsistent, and no case expects it
the CWT sub (a tstr) is compared with instance_subject (a bstr) by the UTF-8 bytes of the tstr, as section 6.1 says "byte-compared with row sub"

ambiguity_log.where: section 9.1 P5, the target at leaf_index
ambiguity_log.reading: TargetStatementMismatch is evaluated when exactly one record holds leaf_index; with two records there, DuplicateIndex already decides

the S2b text defines it by reference to S2a section 6b, which this reading did not open; the rule quoted in StatementPayloadSchemaV0 r9 section 8.11.1 (domain 'P10-LeafEncodeSpecArtifact-v0:', format 'text-markdown-utf-8-v0:', raw bytes) reproduces the pinned value 571765530870e4a6... from frozen/LeafEncodeV0_SPEC.md

ambiguity_log.where: schema r9 section 9 stage 0, protected crit
ambiguity_log.reading: the text requires that a protected crit list only understood parameters but does not list them; this reading understands alg (1), content_type (3) and CWT Claims (15), the protected labels S2b processes, and reads a crit that is not a non-empty array of integers or text strings as a stage-0 failure. SPS-19-crit-ok lists 1, SPS-19-crit-unknown lists 99; understanding alg alone gives the same results, so the vectors do not separate the two lists

ambiguity_log.where: schema r9 section 9, stage 0 on which rows
ambiguity_log.reading: stage 0 (conformant COSE_Sign1, crit, labels 258/259/260) is applied to every row, subject or not, since the table says only stages 1 to 3 are limited to subject entries; no vector has a non-subject row that fails stage 0 alone, so the vectors do not separate this from the subject-only reading

ambiguity_log.where: schema r9 sections 4 and 5, null and numbers
ambiguity_log.reading: 'null is forbidden anywhere in a P10 Statement' and 'no JSON numbers anywhere' are read as whole-Statement rules of stage 1 (row unavailable), also when the null or number sits inside the predicate, not as stage-2 predicate rules (payload = none); SPS-6-number (a number inside ordered_admission_refs) expects the row unavailable

ambiguity_log.where: schema r9 section 8.7 with prereg section 6.2.7, order inside a subject entry
ambiguity_log.reading: stage 0, payload bytes, stage 1, then the signature observation, then stages 2 and 3 (the order of section 8.7's list); so a subject row that fails stage 1 has no observation and its key is not used (no KeyMaterialFingerprintMismatch from it). Prereg 6.2.7 says the bytes feed schema decoding 'after signature processing'; no vector separates the two orders

ambiguity_log.where: schema r9 sections 8.2, 8.4, 8.5, the predicate's instance_subject
ambiguity_log.reading: checked against the CWT sub before S2a only for instance-commitment (section 8.2 says so); for closure the text states no local check (S2a closureAt compares it), and for adjudication the comparison is A1 of AdjudicationBindingV0, after S2a ACCEPT (section 10, SPS-18: binding mutations are expected only after ACCEPT); so neither changes the projection here. Checking it locally for every kind, or for none, gives the same results: the vectors do not separate these readings

ambiguity_log.where: schema r9 section 5, the reference bound
ambiguity_log.reading: a decimal reference above 2^64 - 1 is a stage-2 failure (payload = none), like a reference outside the grammar; both give the same transcript
`first b -> 00 ++ nat(b)`: the boolean b is written nat(0) for false and nat(1) for true, as `bool(b)` is defined two lines above

SHA-256 of the JCS bytes of {"key_resolution": K}, K mapping each iss of frozen.key_resolution to the lowercase hex of its 32-byte fingerprint (the pB form, which the JCS amendment section 9.10 quotes); this reproduces the expected bytes

ambiguity_log.where: prereg section 13.1 with 15.2, rows and entries
ambiguity_log.reading: a non-subject row is available(sub) with the UTF-8 bytes of its sub; a subject row that passes stage 1 is available(sub) and has one detailed entry; a row unreadable at L-B or failing stage 0 or 1 is unavailable

ambiguity_log.where: prereg section 11.2 step 6, the target's wire kind
ambiguity_log.reading: the target's wire kind is the kind derived at schema stage 1, which runs only for subject entries (schema section 9); a target that is not a subject entry, or whose row is unavailable, has no derived kind and gives Invalid(request, TargetKindMismatch). When the target's payload bytes were not obtained, its kind is unknown and no TargetKindMismatch is emitted (StatementPayloadUnavailable stands). SPS-17-nfc-subject (target sub differs from the Unicode instance subject) expects TargetKindMismatch; no vector has a target whose payload is not obtained (in S11 the missing payload is not the target's), so that half of the reading is not separated by the vectors

the case SPS-12-ok-u64max expects Unavailable(capability, VerifierCapabilityUnsupported) from a 64 MiB cap on the encoded transcript; its own note says 'the frozen text sets no limit'; the cap is in the B5 authorization addendum 1 (a build capability). A reader of the frozen text alone has no limit and would produce a transcript; reported, not counted
an empty target_registered_statement_bytes is not encodable (section 7.7); it is reported at P5 as RequestMalformed and P3 is not evaluated, since no candidate entry exists
